# Project Overview & Executive Summary

## Context & Theme
This project, titled **HostelIQ: Smart Hostel Allocation and Occupancy Analytics**, addresses **Theme CAM-07 (Hostel Allocation and Occupancy Planning)** for the B.Tech DSC3132 Business Analytics curriculum.

Residential campus infrastructure represents one of the largest capital and operational commitments in higher education. Mismatches between student housing demand and available physical bed supply create severe operational bottlenecks:
- **Under-allocation / Capacity Deficits:** Leads to prolonged waitlists, student dissatisfaction, and emergency off-campus leasing.
- **Over-allocation / Unoccupied Buffers:** Leads to unamortized capital expenses and wasteful maintenance overheads.

## Primary Analytics Paradigm
The primary analytical classification of this study is **Predictive Analytics**, supported by foundational Descriptive Analytics and downstream Prescriptive Scenario Modeling.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                            HostelIQ Analytics Architecture                        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. Descriptive Analytics    --> 2. Predictive Analytics   --> 3. Prescriptive    |
|  - Occupancy Rates               - 2025-26 Bed Demand          Scenario Modeling  |
|  - Block-wise Distributions        Forecasting                 - Intake Scenarios |
|  - Waitlist Funnel Analysis      - Holdout Validation (MAE)    - Gap Analysis     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Research Question
> **"Can we predict hostel bed demand for the next academic year using historical hostel applications, student intake, occupancy, and room capacity data?"**

---

# Research Objectives & Scope

1. **Quantify Longitudinal Occupancy Patterns:** Evaluate historical bed allocation, vacancy rates, and waitlist pressures across 8 academic years (2017–18 through 2024–25).
2. **Diagnose Infrastructure Bottlenecks:** Identify gender-segregated and block-specific pressure points across campus halls of residence.
3. **Develop Predictive Forecasting Models:**
   - Establish a **Naïve Persistence / Drift baseline**.
   - Construct an **Econometric Multiple Linear Regression (MLR)** model evaluating the elasticity of hostel demand with respect to total student intake and outstation student proportions.
   - Fit an **Univariate Time-Series Exponential Smoothing (Holt’s Linear Trend)** model.
4. **Out-of-Time Model Validation:** Evaluate competing models using holdout test validation (Academic Years 2023–24 and 2024–25) using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).
5. **Conduct Prescriptive Scenario Analysis:** Simulate hostel bed demand under varying university enrollment trajectories ($\pm 10\%$, $+20\%$) and formulate evidence-based allocation guidelines.
6. **Cost per Occupied Bed Assessment (Optional):** Quantify operational efficiency per occupied bed under clearly stated financial assumptions.

---

# Data Architecture & Ethical Governance

## Synthetic Data Declaration & Academic Ethics
> **Notice of Academic Integrity:**  
> In compliance with student privacy regulations and institutional data protection standards, this project utilizes a **statistically calibrated synthetic dataset**.  
> - No authentic student Personally Identifiable Information (PII)—such as student names, registration numbers, contact information, or academic transcripts—is collected or stored.  
> - All synthetic values are algorithmically generated with fixed random seeds for academic reproducibility, reflecting stylized empirical realities of a residential collegiate campus (3,200 beds across 6 residential halls).  
> - Findings and projections represent an academic methodological demonstration rather than real claims regarding any specific university campus.

## Dataset Schemas & Planned Tables

The analytical pipeline is designed to ingest three relational data tables:

1. **`intake_demographics.csv`:** Longitudinal records of annual university admissions, broken down by undergraduate (UG) intake, postgraduate (PG) intake, and outstation student counts.
2. **`hostel_inventory.csv`:** Physical infrastructure inventory specifying hostel designations, gender policies, blocks, room categories (Single/Double/Triple), AC status, and bed capacities.
3. **`annual_hostel_records.csv`:** Annual operational records capturing gross applications, eligible applications, realized bed allocations, waitlisted students, unallocated capacity, and operating costs.

*Detailed variable definitions, data types, units, and integrity constraints are cataloged in [`docs/data_dictionary.md`](docs/data_dictionary.md).*

# Predictive Modeling & Demand Forecasting (Planned Section)

## Modeling Methodology & Candidates
1. **Benchmark Baseline:** Naïve Persistence and Historical Average Drift.
2. **Econometric Model (OLS Multiple Regression):**
   $$\text{BedDemand}_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{OutstationStudents}_t + \beta_2 \cdot \text{TotalIntake}_t + \epsilon_t$$
3. **Time-Series Model:** Holt’s Linear Trend Exponential Smoothing (capturing level and growth trend without overfitting small annual samples).

## Time-Aware Validation Setup
- **Training Set:** Academic Years 2017–18 through 2022–23 ($N=6$).
- **Test Holdout Set:** Academic Years 2023–24 and 2024–25 ($N=2$).
- **Metrics:** MAE, RMSE, MAPE.
